page: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 10 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data positions the E20_v4 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. Single-core stress-ng performance registers at 1412.69, while multi-core performance reaches 18613.51. The memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 1034.46 GB/sec, which drops to 88.48 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression represents a relative performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% tier at 8.63 GB/sec, though multi-threaded decompression recovers to average levels at 66.24 GB/sec.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as relational database operations, in-memory caching, and data processing. Passmark database operations score at 7170.89, and Redis SET operations achieve 16.52 million operations per second. While the instance handles small-scale LLM inference adequately, processing a medium 7B model results in a weak prompt processing speed of 29.26 tokens/sec, highlighting its limitations for complex AI workloads. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
